guidance: A printed vertical line between columns (a column rule) counts as a gap, and the line may run along it.
If there is print on only one side of the line, or on neither (blank paper, the foot of a page), answer Yes as long as the line crosses no print. The dark edge of the scan is not print.
An advertisement, a picture or a heading across several columns counts as print, so a line through one is a No. A line in the gap between two pictures or cartoon panels does run down a gap.
If the line is mostly in a gap but crosses a few letters, answer No.
intro: A program drew a line on each of these crops from English-language pages in Chronicling America, where it thinks two columns of text are separated.
name: English column gutters
question: Does this line run down a gap between columns of text without crossing any printed text?
rules: Say whether the colored line runs down the white gap between two columns without crossing any print. Use Hide the line (L) to see the print under it. You don't need to read the text, only see where the print is.
title: English newspaper column gutters
